description:
We are a group of 5 people participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge with the project "Abandoned but not forgotten".

Our goal is to shine a light on the landers, rovers and probes humanity has left behind on the Moon and Mars - machines that once carried our curiosity to other worlds and now rest silently as part of their landscape. Through this project, we want to honor abandoned explorers  while inspiring next generation of scientist to turning today's fairy tail into tommorow's reality.
summary:
Team Steppe to Space developed “Abandoned but not Forgotten,” an interactive web storytelling platform built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and official NASA/JPL-Caltech data. Guided by Tulpar—a mythical Kazakh winged steed - users spin 3D worlds and fly between the Moon and Mars to visit real abandoned spacecraft, including Surveyor 3, the Apollo 11 retroreflector, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Opportunity, Spirit, and Viking 1, alongside an interactive "The Explorers" archive.

How it addresses the challenge:
Public coverage typically prioritizes active launches, leaving decades of historic hardware buried in dense technical archives and dry textbooks that fail to engage students. Our project transforms silent, discarded machinery into relatable trailblazing heroes through immersive visual storytelling, original sound, and verified NASA mission records.

Why it is important:
It gives teachers a ready-to-use classroom tool for STEM lessons, preserves humanity’s off-world heritage, and connects Kazakhstan’s space legacy - from Baikonur to Kazakh mythology - the stars, inspiring local youth to turn today’s fairy tale into tomorrow’s real mission from the steppe.
details:
Tech Stack: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, custom audio/video production, and Netlify hosting.

NASA Data: Official imagery, orbital photos, and mission records from NASA Science, NASA/JPL-Caltech, NASA Goddard, NASA NSSDC, LRO, and HiRISE.

AI Use: Used AI as a coding assistant during development.
